reason: The cited evidence (E1) directly supports all key premises: it shows that reducing cooling rate creates serrated boundaries, that these boundaries increase tensile fracture strain and creep rupture life (by factors of 3.5 and 400), that they distribute strain more evenly, and that molecular dynamics simulations confirm the mechanism. The hypothesis accurately represents the findings without overstatement.
premises: Serrated grain boundaries improve toughness by distributing strain more evenly and mitigating intergranular crack initiation.
Serrated grain boundaries can be achieved by reducing the cooling rate during solution heat treatment.
The serrated morphology interrupts continuous crack paths and reduces local strain concentration.
The effect is demonstrated in a high-entropy alloy processed by selective laser melting, tested at 650°C.
The mechanism is supported by molecular dynamics simulation showing serrated boundaries distribute strain.
